title: How Bartering Works
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a bit about honey buns as prison currency in Florida state prisons, then turn to bartering: its history from hunter-gatherer trades to settled farming communities, the relative value of goods, timing, triangular and multilateral trades, drawbacks like perishable goods and lopsided trades, why money replaced barter, modern barter revival (Craigslist, craft scene, barter clubs of the late 1970s, barter websites and trade credits), business barter statistics, barter during recession and crises, IRS Form 1099-B reporting rules for barter exchanges, and a closing listener mail segment from Calvin about the etymology of the word mafia.

segments.title: Opening banter and honey buns as prison currency
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck banter, then discuss honey buns as currency and trade goods in Florida state prisons, using a bribe-for-protection example to introduce bartering.

segments.title: History of bartering
segments.summary: The hosts describe bartering as ancient, starting in hunter-gatherer times and taking off once people settled into farming communities with surpluses to trade.

segments.title: Relative value and timing in barter
segments.summary: Barter trades depend on relative value and timing, illustrated by differing values of heaters in hot and cold climates, Richard the Third's horse quote, and a hiking anecdote about Gatorade.

segments.title: Triangular and multilateral barter
segments.summary: Three-way trades (triangular barter, used by NBA teams) and longer multilateral trades are described as ways to complete deals when two people don't directly want each other's goods.

segments.title: Drawbacks of barter and why money replaced it
segments.summary: Barter's drawbacks include the work involved, settling for bad deals under time pressure with perishables, and unequal goods like banquet tables versus tomatoes. Money solved these by being portable, divisible, and standardized.

segments.title: Modern barter revival, barter clubs and trade credits
segments.summary: Modern bartering on Craigslist, in the craft scene, and through services, plus late-1970s barter clubs, online barter sites and trade credits that function as a network currency.

segments.title: Business barter, recessions and disasters
segments.summary: North American companies bartered about twelve billion dollars in goods and services in 2008, up from about 7.75 billion in 2001, with barter rising during recessions, in Argentina around 2009, and after natural disasters.

segments.title: IRS reporting of barter and inflation
segments.summary: Barter exchanges are taxable; the IRS created Form 1099-B after barter clubs grew. Trades can be written off as expenses. The hosts also touch on inflation affecting money and on local economies and secession.

segments.title: Listener mail: Calvin on the word mafia
segments.summary: Calvin writes about the Homie the Clown Simpsons episode and two hypotheses on the origin of the word mafia, from a book by Michael Bradley.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to email trade stories and mention the website and iPhone app.
